s: The Quit India Movement was launched in response to
x: Option (b) is correct: The Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi on 8th August 1942 during the Bombay session of the All-India Congress Committee. It was a response to the Cripps Proposals (March 1942), which Indian leaders viewed as inadequate. The proposals, brought by Sir Stafford Cripps, offered limited dominion status and post-war constitutional reforms, failing to address the immediate demand for complete independence. Mahatma Gandhi called the proposal a post-dated cheque on a tottering bank. Option (a) is incorrect: Proposed in 1946, it aimed to discuss the framework for India's independence, which occurred after the Quit India Movement. Option (c) is incorrect: The Simon Commission Report, formed in 1927 to review India's constitutional system, lacked Indian representation and faced widespread opposition, leading to demands for self-governance. Option (d) is incorrect: At the end of the war, there was tremendous pressure on the British government to break the Indian deadlock (Congress- League disagreement) and present a formula for the future government of India which would be acceptable to both the INC and the All-India Muslim League (AIML). In June 1945, the British government, led by Conservative PM Winston Churchill and the Viceroy, Lord Wavell, simultaneously announced a new offer (Wavell Plan) to work out an interim political agreement under which Indians would be responsible for running the country.

Consider the following statements: Modern Indian History PMF IAS IH – 125
a.
Assertion (A): Lord Linlithgow described the August Movement of 1942 as the most serious rebellion since the Sepoy Mutiny.
b.
Reason (R): There was a massive upsurge of the peasantry in certain areas. Options:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not a correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Linlithgow described the Quit India Movement as the most serious rebellion since the Indian Rebellion of 1857. The movement witnessed widespread participation, including massive peasant uprisings in several regions, attacks on communication networks, and the establishment of parallel governments. Hence, the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

s:
Assertion (A) : Lord Linlithgow described the August Movement of 1942 as the most serious rebellion since Sepoy Mutiny.
Reason (R) : There was a massive upsurge of the peasantry in certain areas.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not a correct
x: The involvement of peasants in Quit India Movement made the struggle more violent. This forced Linlithgow to describe the Quit India Movement launched on 9th August, 1942 A.D. as the most serious rebellion since Sepoy Mutiny of 1857. Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

s: During which movement the two brothers Gangaram and Kheemdev were martyred?
x: The two brothers Gangaram and Kheemdev were martyred during Quit India Movement in 1942 A.D. during Police firing at Almora. Note : In dictionary of Martyrs Vol.-2, they are mentioned as Gangadutt and Kheemananda.

s: Baldev Sahai resigned from the post of advocate general in –
x: Under operation zero hour, Indian leaders were arrested during Quit India Movement. To protest this and other oppressive acts of government, Baldev Sahai resigned in 1942 from the post of advocate general.

s: Which one of the following observations is not true about the Quit India Movement of 1942?
o: It was led by Mahatma Gandhi
It did not attract the labour class in general
x: The Quit India Movement did attract the labour class, so the statement that it did not is the untrue observation.

s: Who among the following called the Movements of Gandhiji as ‘Political Blackmail’?
x: Lord Linlithgow called the Movement of Gandhi as ‘Political Blackmail.’ Viceroy and Governor-General Lord Linlithgow’s tenure was the longest in India. He was the longest-serving Viceroy of India from 1936 to 1943. Quit India Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi during his tenure. Quit India Movement *During 5-14 July, 1942 A.D., a meeting of Congress Committee was held at Wardha. It was attended by prominent leaders of Congress like Jawahar Lal Nehru, Abul Kalam Azad, Vallabh Bhai Patel, Mahatma Gandhi, Aruna Asaf Ali, Achyut Patwardhan, Dr. Anugrah Narayan Sinha, Pattabhi Sitaramayya etc. *‘Quit India’ resolution was passed in this meeting on July 14, 1942. It was chaired by then Congress President Abul Kalam Azad. *On 7th -8th August, 1942 A.D., meeting of All India Congress Committee was held at Gowalia Tank (now August Kranti ground) in Bombay. Wardha Resolution was confirmed in this meeting. *After a few modifications, the resolution for Quit India movement was passed on 8th August, 1942 A.D. Quit India Movement for India’s Independence was launched on 9th August 1942. Gandhiji gave a statement before the official launch of Quit India Movement. The statement had the following important points. 1) Government officials should announce their support and devotion to Congress. 2) Soldiers should refuse to fire on their countrymen. 3) Students should quit studies only if they stood firmly on this decision until independence. 4) Kings should accept the sovereignty of their

s: Which of the following statements is NOT true about the "Quit India Movement of 1942"?
o: It was led by Mahatma Gandhi
Congress was declared an illegal body
x: Quit India is treated as a spontaneous mass movement (UPSC 2011 counts 'spontaneous' as true), the Congress committees were declared unlawful and Gandhi led it, but violence became widespread after the leaders' arrest, so 'it was a non-violent movement' is the NOT-true statement.

s: During the freedom struggle, Aruna Asaf Ali was a major woman organiser of underground activity in which of the following movements?
x: Aruna Asaf Ali played a prominent role during the Quit India Movement (1942). After the arrest of several major Congress leaders, she emerged as a key figure in the underground resistance. She is best remembered for hoisting the Indian National Flag at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 9 August 1942. When the movement was brutally suppressed, she went underground and helped organise secret networks, distribute pamphlets, and coordinate resistance activities. Her role made her a symbol of courage and defiance, earning her the title "Grand Old Lady of the Indian Independence Movement."

s: In which context did Jai Prakash Narayan gain recognition of national leader?
o: Making the member of Congress Executive Committee
x: Jaya Prakash Narayan gained recognition as a national leader during Quit India Movement. All the main leaders of Congress were arrested in the start of the movement. Congress leaders who couldn’t be arrested started to consolidate public secretly. Jaya Prakash Narayan, Ram Manohar Lohia, and Aruna Asaf Ali were the main leaders among them.

s: During the Quit India Movement, a girl named Kanaklata Barua led a public procession and defying the police, tried to enter the police station but was shot dead. This incident took place at –
x: Kanaklata Barua was an Indian Independence fighter who was shot dead by British police while leading a procession during Quit India Movement of 1942 A.D. She was shot when she tried to hoist national flag at the local police station of the Gohpur subdivision of Sonitpur district, Assam.

s: Who among the following women freedom fighters was not associated with 'Quit India Movement'?
x: Matangini Hazra was 73 years old when she fell to British bullets, leading a protest March in 1942 A.D. in Tamluk, Bengal during the Quit India Movement. Kanaklata Barua was an Indian freedom fighter and AISF leader. She joined the Mrityu Bahini ('Death Army'), a death squad comprising group of youth from the Gohpur sub-division of Assam in line with Gandhiji's 'Do or Die' call during 'Quit India Movement'. She was shot dead in September 1942 while bearing the National flag at age of about 17 in Borangabari, Gohpur, Assam. Aruna Asaf Ali was an Indian educator, political activist and publisher. An active participant in the Indian Independence movement, she is widely remembered for hoisting the Indian National Flag at the Gowalia Tank maidan (now August Kranti Ground), Bombay (Mumbai) during Quit India Movement in 1942 A.D. Shanti Ghosh was an active member of the revolutionary group, Yugantar. On 14th December, 1931 A.D. Shanti Ghosh along with Suniti entered the bungalow of a District Magistrate with a pistol and shot him dead at point-blank range. Hence, option (d) is correct answer.

s: With reference to 8 th August, 1942 in Indian history, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The Quit India Resolution was adopted by the AICC.
The Viceroy's Executive Council was expanded to include more Indians.
The Congress ministries resigned in seven provinces.
Cripps proposed an Indian Union with full Dominion Status once the Second World War was over.
x: The failure of the Cripps Mission made it clear that Britain was not ready to give India any real Constitutional advance. In May 1942, Gandhiji drafted a resolution calling for British withdrawal and non-violent noncooperation in the face of any Japanese invasion. In July, the Congress Working Committee (CWC) at Wardha adopted the Resolution (later known as the Quit India Resolution), which was to be ratified at the Bombay All India Congress Committee (AICC) meeting in August. On 8 th August 1942, the AICC at Gowalia Tank in Bombay, passed a historic Quit India resolution. The resolution demanded an immediate end to British rule in India. Subsequently, on 9 th August 1942, the British Government, invoking the Defence of India Rules, arrested Gandhi along with members of the Congress Working Committee and other leaders. The Working Committee, the All- India Congress Committee, and the four Provincial Congress Committees were deemed illegal associations under the Criminal Law Amendment Act of 1908.

The Kurnool Circular was prepared by Kala Venkata Rao, an eminent freedom fighter and Congress leader from Andhra. The circular provided guidance to Congress workers regarding organizational strategy during the freedom movement. It became an important document in strengthening nationalist activities in the Andhra region. Kala Venkata Rao later emerged as one of the leading political figures of Andhra Pradesh.
